sentences.zh: 在这场大火中摧毁的众多珍宝中，包括元老院大楼以及君士坦丁在很久以前用于装饰浴室的古老雕像。

sentences.en: We're in the sixth century.

sentences.en: We're in Constantinople, the new Rome, the capital of the, well, you call it the Roman Empire, the Eastern Roman Empire, the Byzantine Empire.
sentences.zh: 我们身处君士坦丁堡，也就是新罗马，这个……嗯，你称之为罗马帝国、东罗马帝国、拜占庭帝国的首都。

sentences.en: This incredibly glamorous couple are emperor and empress, Justinian and Theodore.
sentences.zh: 这对极其光鲜亮丽的夫妇就是皇帝和皇后，查士丁尼和狄奥多拉。

sentences.en: They have just seen off the blues and the greens, the circus factions who are rioting at the beginning of 532.
sentences.zh: 他们刚刚击退了蓝党和绿党——也就是在532年之初引发暴动的竞技场派系。

sentences.en: Justinian is rebuilding Hagia Sophia, the great church of the Holy Wisdom, the great cathedral that still is one of the world's great sort of tourist sites in the center of
sentences.zh: 查士丁尼正在重建圣索菲亚大教堂，这座伟大的圣智教堂，直到今天它依然是位于伊斯坦布尔中心的

sentences.en: Istanbul.

sentences.zh: 汤姆，查士丁尼，我的意思是，正如你所说，查士丁尼的矛盾之处在于，在传统上，我想在通俗的

sentences.zh: 历史书、教科书和百科全书之类的内容中，他似乎标志着与古代罗马的决裂，六世纪大致是人们不再称其为罗马帝国，转而开始称

sentences.zh: 其为拜占庭帝国的节点。

sentences.en: But Justinian has this project, doesn't he, to rebuild not just the city, but to rebuild the Roman world by reuniting Constantinople with Italy and with
sentences.zh: 但查士丁尼有一个宏伟的计划，不是吗？不仅要重建这座城市，还要通过将君士坦丁堡与意大利、

sentences.en: North Africa and perhaps ultimately with Spain, who knows, with Gaul, with Britain even, with the provinces that have been loSt. Yeah.

sentences.en: And I think this is, we talked about, we ended our last episode on this note that Justinian is an incredibly paradoxical figure because on the one hand,
sentences.zh: 我想这也是，我们谈到了——我们在上一集的结尾也提到了这一点，即查士丁尼是一个极其矛盾的人物，因为一方面，

sentences.en: he seems almost a bit of an anachronism.
sentences.zh: 他看起来几乎有点不合时宜。

sentences.en: He is a kind of Caesar of the order of Trajan.
sentences.zh: 他是一种图拉真级别的凯撒。

sentences.en: He's a great conqueror.
sentences.zh: 他是一位伟大的征服者。

sentences.en: He's the embodiment of these kind of ancient Roman martial imperial traditions.
sentences.zh: 他是这种古老罗马尚武帝国传统的化身。

sentences.en: But at the same time, his attempts to kind of restore this Roman Empire actually precipitates its decline.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他试图恢复这个罗马帝国的举动，实际上却加速了它的衰落。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, that's the big, that's the big argument, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 好吧，这才是那个宏大的、最核心的论点，不是吗？

sentences.en: About whether that's the case.
sentences.zh: 关于这是否属实。

sentences.en: But actually when it starts, so he starts with North Africa, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 但实际上当它开始时，他是从北非开始的，对吧？

sentences.zh: 那是第一个目标。

sentences.zh: 而且这个地方相对来说……我的意思是，它大约被一群被称为汪达尔人的人统治了一百年。

sentences.en: And actually that, that campaign goes pretty well.
sentences.zh: 实际上，那场战役进展得相当顺利。

sentences.en: The Vandals, interestingly, we've, we haven't talked as much as some people might expect about
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，关于汪达尔人，我们并没有像某些人可能期望的那样，过多地讨论

sentences.zh: 基督论的争端。

sentences.zh: 但汪达尔人其实是又一种异端，因为他们是阿里乌派，对吧？

sentences.en: So they believe now, Tom, I know you'll think this is grotesque simplification, but am I right in thinking the Vandals believe that Jesus is subordinate to God?
sentences.zh: 所以他们相信……现在，汤姆，我知道你会觉得这是一种极大的简化，但我认为汪达尔人相信耶稣从属于上帝，这种想法对吗？

sentences.en: Basically, yes.
sentences.zh: 基本上是的。

sentences.en: He's not, he's not co-eternal with God.
sentences.zh: 他与上帝并非同永恒。

sentences.en: He's not quite as good.
sentences.zh: 他没有那么崇高。

sentences.en: And so we, in the first episode, we talked about these kind of rounds about the nature of Christ
sentences.zh: 所以在第一集里，我们讨论了这些关于基督本质的争论，

sentences.en: and the Aryan heresy that the Vandals hold to is a product of the fourth century, the age of

sentences.en: Constantine.
sentences.zh: 君士坦丁。

sentences.en: So in that sense, the Vandals are, you know, they're throwbacks, they're theological throwbacks.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，汪达尔人，你知道的，他们是历史的倒退者，是神学上的老古董。

sentences.en: Crikey.

sentences.en: So they've clearly, you know, they've got to be cleared up.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，你知道的，他们必须被清除。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 汪达尔人构成了双重威胁，因为他们占领了曾经养活罗马的粮仓。

sentences.en: They're occupying the great Roman city of Carthage.
sentences.zh: 他们占领了伟大的罗马城市迦太基。

sentences.en: Um, but also they hold to this kind of antiquated heresy and, uh, it's unacceptable.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且他们还坚持这种陈旧的异端邪说，呃，这是不可接受的。

sentences.en: So Justinian raises an immense fleet, a great armada.
sentences.zh: 因此，查士丁尼组建了一支庞大的舰队，一支伟大的无敌舰队。

sentences.zh: 它在欢呼声中从君士坦丁堡港口起航，并取得了巨大的成功。

sentences.en: The equivalents of loads of unarmed football hooligans.

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.zh: 嗯，不过话说回来，当你看看时间线，舰队是在533年盛夏出发的。

sentences.en: So that's just over a year, a year and a bit since the, the end of the rioting.
sentences.zh: 所以那刚好在暴乱结束一年多一点的时候。

sentences.en: Um, but actually they pretty much wiped the floor with the Vandals within less than a year.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但实际上他们在不到一年的时间里就把汪达尔人打得落花流水。

sentences.en: Uh, so that the, the, the king of the Vandals is a man called Gelimer.
sentences.zh: 呃，所以汪达尔人的国王是一个叫盖利摩的人。

sentences.en: Do you know what happened to Gelimer, Tom?
sentences.zh: 你知道盖利摩后来怎么了吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: He gets taken back, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他被带回去了，对吧？

sentences.en: And led in triumph.
sentences.zh: 并在凯旋仪式上游街示众。

sentences.en: So he was beaten at a battle.
sentences.zh: 所以他是在一场战役中战败了。

sentences.zh: 盖利摩去躲藏了起来，呃，贝利撒留说，你投降吗？

sentences.en: And he said, yes.
sentences.zh: 而他说，我投降。

sentences.en: And do you know what he asked for in return?
sentences.zh: 你知道他要求什么作为回报吗？

sentences.en: I'm so delighted.
sentences.zh: 我太高兴了。

sentences.en: I found these details.
sentences.zh: 我发现了这些细节。

sentences.zh: 他说，我只需要两样东西就能让我投降。

sentences.en: The sponge was to wipe his eye because he'd, he suffered an eye infection while in hiding.

sentences.en: He'd written a dirge because he felt very downbeat after losing his kingdom.
sentences.zh: 他写了一首哀歌，因为在失去王国后他感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: And he said, I'd like a liar so that I could, I could try it out.
sentences.zh: 他说，我想要一把里拉琴，这样我可以弹奏它、尝试一下。

sentences.en: So Belisarius gave him that.
sentences.zh: 于是贝利撒留满足了他。

sentences.en: So he gave him the sponge and the liar.
sentences.zh: 所以他给了他海绵和里拉琴。

sentences.en: He was taken to Constantinople in, and he was led in a triumph.
sentences.zh: 他被带到了君士坦丁堡，并在凯旋仪式上被游街示众。

sentences.en: So that's very Roman, Tom.

sentences.zh: 我想加拉太现在是在土耳其吧？

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's kind of middle of Cappadocia.
sentences.zh: 所以它大概在卡帕多西亚的中部。

sentences.en: So is, is he, is he, is he in danger of getting a letter from St. Paul?
sentences.zh: 那么，他、他、他有没有收到圣保罗信件的危险？

sentences.en: Did St. Paul write to the, did he write to the Galatians?
sentences.zh: 圣保罗写信给……他写信给加拉太人了吗？

sentences.zh: 是的，他写过。

sentences.zh: 嗯，那我这样想对不对：汪达尔人在非洲的统治一定相对来说比较肤浅？

sentences.en: So, um, and the story is, is that they, they took the, um, the looted treasures from Jerusalem that Titus had brought in, uh,

sentences.en: We're celebrating triumphs.

sentences.en: And yeah,
sentences.zh: 而且是的，

sentences.zh: 在这些战争的某个时期，罗马实际上变得荒无人烟。

sentences.en: So the city that at the heyday of the empire had had a million, you know, it's, it's this absolute wilderness.

sentences.en: It's this emptied wilderness.
sentences.zh: 这是一片被掏空的荒野。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，意大利的大部分地区都是如此，对吧？

sentences.zh: 农田被这些来回穿梭交错的军队摧毁了。

sentences.en: I mean, it must've been a kind of apocalyptic landscape.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那一定是一种末日般的景象。

sentences.zh: 如果你想问，罗马帝国究竟是什么时候在

sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你是罗马的元老，最后却成了一个身无分文的难民，这根本算不上什么安慰，你知道的，你现在是被一个

sentences.zh: 并且夺走了意大利的大片土地，以至于君士坦丁堡最终仍然统治着罗马。

sentences.zh: 所以它依然拥有罗马，也拥有拉韦纳，因为拉韦纳是一个向亚得里亚海航运开放的港口。

sentences.zh: 而且拉韦纳之前也是一个帝国的首都，对吧？

sentences.zh: 是的，曾经是。

sentences.zh: 所以那里有很多宫殿。

sentences.zh: 从现代游客的角度来看，这些战争是非常值得的，因为这些

sentences.en: In Ravenna.
sentences.zh: 在拉韦纳。

sentences.en: Irene, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 伊琳娜，也许吧。

sentences.en: Irene, yeah.
sentences.zh: 伊琳娜，是的。

sentences.en: But apart from that, nobody remembers other empresses.

sentences.zh: 是的，我确信。

sentences.en: Because, you know, the literal iconography of it, it's so powerful.

sentences.en: And they're such kind of stunning mosaics.
sentences.zh: 而且它们是如此惊艳的马赛克壁画。

sentences.en: They're such kind of, you know, they're on the cover of every book about, not just Justinian and Theodora, but about pretty much Byzantium.
sentences.zh: 它们就像是，你知道的，出现在每一本关于查士丁尼和狄奥多拉的书的封面上，甚至几乎是每一本关于拜占庭帝国的书的封面。

sentences.en: Well, I think because they're completely worth it and a tremendous idea, because they gave us the mosaics that we can advertise this podcast with.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我认为这是完全值得的，而且是一个了不起的主意，因为它们为我们提供了可以用作这个播客宣传画的马赛克壁画。

sentences.zh: 然而，就在他们刚刚踏上征程之后，我的意思是，在开始重新征服

sentences.zh: 所以也许他是肯尼迪。

sentences.zh: 总之，波斯人再次出现，跨过边境，基本上攻占了安条克。

sentences.zh: 它是叙利亚的伟大首都。

sentences.zh: 所以这是一场灾难。

sentences.zh: 正如你所说，没有——正如你在之前的节目中所说，在

sentences.zh: 但这对于查士丁尼来说是一个巨大的挫折。

sentences.zh: 你觉得呢？

sentences.en: So we talked about this with Kyle last week.
sentences.zh: 所以我们上周和凯尔讨论过这个。

sentences.en: So it comes to the plague arrives, hits Pelusium, hits Alexandria, winnows out from Alexandria to Constantinople and then to Italy and then onwards, westwards and eastwards.

sentences.en: I mean, Procopius says 10,000 people a day died in Constantinople.

sentences.zh: 所以人们会说，啊，
